title: Conflict-Aware Hybrid RAG for Mitigating LLM Hallucination in Educational Question Answering
content: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds large language models (LLMs) in external evidence, yet hallucination persists when retrieved passages conflict with the model's parametric knowledge. This study proposes a conflict-aware hybrid RAG framework that combines lexical and dense retrieval, a domain-adapted LLM-based reranker fine-tuned with low-rank adaptation, and a conflict detection module that checks draft answers against retrieved evidence before regenerating or abstaining. The framework is evaluated on an academic knowledge base built from university regulations, curricula and policy documents in a Kenyan higher-education setting. The benchmark contains 300 question–answer pairs, 30% of which are designed so that institution-specific rules contradict general knowledge. We compare the framework with closed-book LLMs, standard dense RAG and hybrid RAG using open-weight and commercial models, measuring accuracy, faithfulness, citation precision and recall, abstention quality and latency. We hypothesise that the framework reduces hallucination and improves citation precision over standard RAG, with the largest gains expected on conflict questions, at a modest latency cost. Such results would indicate that explicitly managing knowledge conflicts is essential for trustworthy RAG-based decision support in education. We also discuss fairness, transparency and deployment considerations for low-resource institutions.
